question: How is Raymond James positioning itself to recruit advisors away from the wirehouses?

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Raymond James' CEO describes the firm as offering the largest addressable market across its affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to RIA custody, and notes advisors are coming from wires, regionals, and other independents; the value proposition of cultural fit, platform, and multiple affiliation options appeals to advisors from many firms.

Raymond James Financial: The firm describes its differentiated value proposition as advisors not having to choose between culture and capabilities, offering a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology, products, and solutions.

Raymond James Financial: The firm states it does not lead with the highest check but leads with culture and capabilities, maintaining a differentiated value proposition and remaining disciplined on transition assistance and economics.

Raymond James Financial: The firm describes its best-of-both-worlds value proposition, combining an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology and solutions, and cites its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence as a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

Raymond James Financial: The CEO states the firm has the largest total addressable market by having all affiliation options at scale, so advisors moving do not have to consider whether Raymond James offers a channel but only whether they are a cultural fit.

Raymond James Financial: The firm states it has the largest addressable market because it has all affiliation options an advisor could want, and it is agnostic to how advisors affiliate, wanting them to embrace its culture, values, platform, and capabilities.

Raymond James Financial: The firm's recruiting pages describe the AdvisorChoice platform as offering advisors the ability to match professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, each backed by a leading independent financial firm.

Raymond James Financial: During the fiscal third quarter ended June 30, 2026, Raymond James recruited financial advisers to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production totaling $156 million.

Raymond James Financial: During the fiscal third quarter ended June 30, 2026, Raymond James recruited financial advisers to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels representing nearly $23 billion of client assets at their previous firms.
Raymond James Financial: Through the first nine months of fiscal 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), Raymond James recruited advisers with trailing 12-month production totaling $393 million.

Raymond James Financial: Through the first nine months of fiscal 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), Raymond James recruited advisers representing more than $56 billion of client assets at their previous firms.

Raymond James Financial: In the fiscal second quarter (ended March 31, 2026), Raymond James recruited financial advisers to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production totaling $141 million.

Raymond James Financial: In the fiscal second quarter (ended March 31, 2026), Raymond James recruited financial advisers to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels representing nearly $21 billion of client assets at their previous firms.
Raymond James Financial: In the last 12 months (as of December 31, 2025), Raymond James recruited advisors who had $460 million in production at their prior firms.

Raymond James Financial: Over the prior 12 months (as of December 31, 2024), Raymond James recruited financial advisors with approximately $318 million of trailing 12-month production and $51 billion of client assets at their previous firms to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels.

Raymond James Financial: Over the prior 12 months (as of December 31, 2024), including assets recruited into the RIA and Custody Services Division, Raymond James recruited total client assets of nearly $61 billion across all of its platforms.

Raymond James Financial: Over the past 12 months (as of March 31, 2025), Raymond James recruited into its domestic independent contractor and employee channels financial advisors with approximately $316 million of trailing 12-month production and $50 billion of client assets at their previous firms.
Raymond James Financial: In fiscal 2025, Raymond James recruited production advisors with prior production of over $400 million, up 21% over the prior year's record.

Raymond James Financial: For the full fiscal 2026 year, Raymond James reported trailing 12-month production of $538 million for recruited advisors coming into its domestic independent contractor and employee channels, up from $407 million the prior year, representing more than $82 billion in client assets.

Raymond James Financial: Trade press reports that Raymond James & Associates added a two-advisor team from Truist Investment Services with more than $1.2 billion in client assets to its employee advisor channel.
Raymond James Financial: Trade press reports that Raymond James & Associates welcomed a three-advisor team from PNC Private Bank that managed over $1.5 billion in client assets.
Raymond James Financial: Trade press reports that Raymond James & Associates added a team from UBS Financial Services that previously managed more than $550 million in client assets.
Raymond James Financial: Trade press reports that Raymond James added a Wells Fargo advisor who managed more than $160 million in client assets to Raymond James Financial Services.

Raymond James Financial: Trade press reports that Raymond James recruited a team of advisors from Truist Investment Services managing about $700 million in client assets to its Financial Institutions Division.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James positions its value proposition as a best of both worlds offering: a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, which it says resonates with advisors across all affiliation options.

Raymond James Financial: The firm states its value proposition, coupled with its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence, is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James describes a powerfully personal value proposition focused on personal relationships with financial advisors and giving them tools and resources to strengthen their client relationships, in contrast to competitors it says focus on IRRs and exit periods.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James states that 100% of what it pays in transition assistance goes to advisor retention rather than to a seller, contrasting one-by-one recruiting with acquisitions.

Raymond James Financial: The firm says it does not lead with the highest check but offers competitive economics while leading with culture and capabilities, remaining disciplined on transition assistance and advisor economics.

Raymond James Financial: The firm defines PCG recruiting and retention-related compensation as including cash and equity awards issued in conjunction with recruiting activities, as retention for existing advisors, or in conjunction with acquisitions, expensed over a requisite service period typically between 5 and 10 years.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James originates loans to financial advisors primarily as part of its recruiting activities.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James emphasizes advisor book ownership as central to its employee advisor offering, describing your business, your brand, your clients.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James participates, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs the client information financial advisors may take when affiliating with a new firm and their ability to solicit clients of their prior firm.
Raymond James Financial: The firm lists a payout of up to 50% plus a full array of competitive employee benefits for the Traditional Employee affiliation model (page content as of 2026-04-21).
Raymond James Financial: The firm lists a 70-80% gross payout plus a full array of competitive employee benefits for the Advisor Select affiliation model (page content as of 2026-04-21).
Raymond James Financial: The firm lists an 81% to 90% payout for the Independent Contractor affiliation model (page content as of 2026-04-21).

Raymond James Financial: The firm's competitive pay packages include base salary, incentive bonus, and equity compensation programs, and it may grant equity awards in connection with initial employment.

Raymond James Financial: In fiscal 2025, adjusted compensation expense included amortization of transition assistance provided to recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors in the aggregate amount of $355 million, up approximately 11% versus fiscal 2024.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James states its advisors are coming from wires, regionals, and other independents, and that its value proposition, cultural fit, platform, and multiple affiliation options appeal to advisors from many different firms.

Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2025, Raymond James reported a total of 8,943 financial advisors (3,878 employees and 5,065 independent contractors); advisors in its RCS division are not included in the financial advisor metric.
Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2024, Raymond James reported a total of 8,787 financial advisors (3,826 employees and 4,961 independent contractors).
Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2023, Raymond James reported a total of 8,712 financial advisors (3,693 employees and 5,019 independent contractors).
Raymond James Financial: As of March 31, 2025, Raymond James reported approximately 8,731 financial advisors, per its investor day deck.
Raymond James Financial: In fiscal year 2019, Raymond James reported approximately 8,011 financial advisors, per its investor day deck.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James stated that the number of financial advisors as of September 30, 2025 increased compared to the prior year, as new recruits and trainees moved into production roles exceeded departures and planned retirements.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James ended fiscal year 2025 with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year, which it attributed to solid advisor retention and strong recruiting results.

Raymond James Financial: CEO Paul Shoukry stated that the financial advisor recruiting pipeline remains strong and is broad-based, drawing advisers from many different firms and communities interested in the variety of affiliation options, and is not driven by one firm, catalyst, or affiliation option (period ended June 30, 2026). Why it might matter: management attributed the strong recruiting results and broad-based pipeline to coupling capabilities with being one of those firms, in the context of its differentiated value proposition.

Raymond James Financial: CEO Paul Shoukry stated that as the firm enters the fiscal fourth quarter it does so with significant momentum supported by historically strong business drivers and robust financial adviser recruiting (period ended June 30, 2026). Why it might matter: this momentum follows record revenues, record pre-tax income and record earnings per share in the first 9 months of the fiscal year.

Raymond James Financial: In the fiscal third quarter ended June 30, 2026, Raymond James recruited financial advisers to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production totaling $156 million. Why it might matter: the firm described itself as a destination of choice for financial advisers across its affiliation options, noting domestic net new assets of $21.7 billion in the fiscal third quarter.

Raymond James Financial: In the fiscal third quarter ended June 30, 2026, Raymond James recruited financial advisers to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels representing nearly $23 billion of client assets at their previous firms. Why it might matter: this came in a quarter where the firm reported domestic net new assets of $21.7 billion, representing a 5.5% annualized growth rate.

Raymond James Financial: Through the first nine months of fiscal 2026, Raymond James recruited advisers with trailing 12-month production totaling $393 million, putting the firm on a clear path to exceed the record results set in fiscal 2025. Why it might matter: the prior fiscal year's record was over $400 million of prior production, up 21% over the prior year's record.

Raymond James Financial: Through the first nine months of fiscal 2026, Raymond James recruited advisers representing more than $56 billion of client assets at their previous firms. Why it might matter: this recruiting success reflects what the firm calls its differentiated value proposition, that advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities.

Raymond James Financial: CEO Paul Shoukry stated that the source of this year's recruiting success as well as the current pipeline remains diverse across the firm's affiliation options (period ended June 30, 2026). Why it might matter: the strength in retaining and attracting high-quality advisers reflects the differentiated value proposition in which advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities.

Raymond James Financial: CEO Paul Shoukry stated that net new asset growth for the fiscal year so far is up 119%, with $75 billion of net new assets, up from last year which was a record (period ended June 30, 2026). Why it might matter: the CEO said this growth starts with keeping existing advisers satisfied and having high retention of existing advisers.

Raymond James Financial: Trade press reports that an Ohio hire extends a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026, as wirehouse advisors respond to changes in how UBS compensates its advisor workforce (2026). Why it might matter: Raymond James ended fiscal year 2025 with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year, which it attributed to solid advisor retention and strong recruiting results.

Raymond James Financial: Trade press reports that earlier in 2026 Raymond James brought on breakaway teams from Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley whose combined assets exceeded $1 billion (2026). Why it might matter: the report describes this as part of a sustained recruitment drive that has seen the firm pull talent from across the wirehouse and regional broker-dealer landscape.

Raymond James Financial: Trade press reports that a team that previously managed more than $550 million in client assets at UBS Financial Services joined Raymond James in The Woodlands, Texas (2026). Why it might matter: the trade press also reports Raymond James recruited a team of advisors from Truist Investment Services managing about $700 million in client assets to its Financial Institutions Division.

Raymond James Financial: The comparison of the firm's recruiting appeal and wirehouse advisor wins against competitors or prior periods can be made in part only. The firm's own prior-period comparisons are valid: through the first nine months of fiscal 2026 it recruited $393 million of trailing 12-month production versus a fiscal 2025 record of over $400 million, and trade press reports fiscal 2026 production of $538 million versus $407 million the prior year. However, direct comparisons to competitors are not valid on this evidence: the sources provide no comparable recruiting figures for other firms; the 97% advisor satisfaction rate and the 7% annualized net new assets figure are the firm's own claims about the industry, not independently sourced competitor figures.
